issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem 3.3 contains multiple fundamental mathematical failures: (1) It constructs \bar u by prescribing terminal condition \bar u(T) = z_0 for the forward semilinear heat equation. The backward Cauchy problem for the heat equation with arbitrary L^2 data is severely ill-posed and solutions generally do not exist; the cited sources establish well-posedness only for the initial value problem forward in time. (2) It applies Grönwall's inequality backwards in time to the differential inequality \partial_t \|\hat u\|^2 \le C_0 \|\hat u\|^2 + \dots in (3.6) to infer an upper bound on \|\hat u(t)\|^2 in terms of \|\hat u(T)\|^2; integrating y'(t) \le C y(t) backwards from T yields a lower bound on y(t), not an upper bound. (3) It applies the controllability estimate of Fernandez-Cara & Guerrero (2006, Theorem 1.6) in (3.9) to claim \|f - f_{\bar\theta}\|_{L^2(q_T)} \le C_2 \|u_0 - \bar u(0)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}. Controllability theorems only guarantee the existence of at least one control (the HUM/minimal control) satisfying that bound, not that an arbitrary control difference f - f_{\bar\theta} satisfies it. Moreover, exact controls are non-unique, so the claim that any PINN minimizer converges to the control f is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must avoid the ill-posed backward heat equation, address the non-uniqueness of controls by selecting and penalizing a specific control norm, and establish valid stability estimates relating residuals to state and control errors.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.3 is completely invalidated. There is no supported guarantee that driving the WeightedPINN loss to zero yields convergence of either the neural network state u_\theta or the control f_{\bar\theta} to the true solution u and control f.
issues.title: Ill-posed backward heat equation and invalid Grönwall and controllability inferences in Theorem 3.3
issues.why_classification: Theorem 3.3 is a central theoretical result of the paper. Its proof fails due to the ill-posedness of the backward heat equation, an invalid backward Grönwall inference, and a misapplied controllability estimate. No comparable result can be salvaged without essentially new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: In (3.17), the proof applies Theorem 4.1 of Zuazua (2024) to deduce that \|f - f_{\bar\theta}\|_{L^2(q_T)} is bounded by the initial state discrepancy \|u_0 - \bar u(0)\|_{H^1} + \|u_1 - \partial_t \bar u(0)\|_{L^2}. This inference is invalid: controllability theorems only assert the existence of at least one control steering the state to zero that satisfies such an estimate (such as the minimal L^2-norm control). The difference f - f_{\bar\theta} between an arbitrary exact control f and the trained neural network f_{\bar\theta} is not that minimal control. Furthermore, exact internal controls for the semilinear wave equation are not unique (there exists an infinite-dimensional space of controls steering (0,0) to (0,0)), and different exact controls produce different state trajectories. A neural network minimizing the PDE residual cannot be guaranteed to converge to an arbitrarily chosen control f or its trajectory u.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must formulate a criterion that singles out a unique control (such as minimal L^2 norm), incorporate that selection mechanism into the PINN objective, and establish a valid stability bound relating the residual to the chosen control.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.4 is invalidated; the convergence guarantee for the WeightedPINN approximation of the state and control of the wave equation is unsupported and false as stated.
issues.title: Invalid inference from controllability theorem and non-uniqueness of controls in Theorem 3.4
issues.why_classification: Theorem 3.4 is a main convergence result. Because controls are non-unique and arbitrary control differences do not satisfy controllability bounds, the claim is false and cannot be repaired within the existing framework without altering the objective and proof architecture.
